meta.q:
Minecraft AI 伙伴（Java mod，能在游戏里自己挖矿/合成/战斗）的诊断求助，请给要点不要客套：

【现象】我们给它换了一个新 LLM（thinking 很重的模型，单轮输出 1万+ token），结果它 2分半钟内连续死了

text:
The user asks: can this phenomenon be confirmed as a "model problem" rather than our code problem? Is the causal chain "56% compression + tool param format errors + repeated deaths" valid?
They want direct points, no pleasantries. I need to be honest and precise: it's NOT purely a model problem. The causal chain partially holds but misattributes root cause.
Key analysis:
"模型问题"这个定性是错的 / 至少是误导的。 Three distinct things:
a) 工具参数格式错误 (Expected BEGIN_ARRAY): This one IS closest to a model-side issue — the model emitting malformed JSON or truncation. BUT: even here, your code owns the contract: did you validate schema before sending? Is max_tokens sufficient? Does your prompt/tool spec match what the model expects? If the old model works and new one fails, could be the new model's tool-calling training format mismatch (e.g., model fine-tuned on a different tool schema convention). You can fix via: better tool spec in prompt, stricter JSON schema, repair retry. So it's a "model capability/format compliance issue" that your code must defensively handle. Attribution: ~70% model, 30% your integration (insufficient max_tokens, no validation/repair).
b) 压缩占比 56%: This is NOT a model problem. Context management is 100% your code. The model only produces tokens; what you put in context, when you compress, what's retained — all your pipeline. Also, why does compression correlate with death? Because compression is triggered by context size and blocks the loop. The compression ratio being high just reflects long outputs — but the decision to count compression calls as "calls", to run compression synchronously, to not pin critical state — all code.
c) 反复死亡: This is an architecture problem. The model doesn't control the game loop directly; your code decides to block waiting for LLM output, has no reflex layer, no safety state, no item recovery timer. Even a perfect model with 30s latency would cause deaths under this architecture. Actually a dumb-but-fast model survives; a smart-but-slow one dies — that proves the architecture depends on latency luck, not intelligence. So deaths = your code's fault in system design.
因果链是否成立? Partially:
"工具格式错误 → 该轮动作作废 → 发呆窗口" — holds, minor contributor (6 errors in 2.5 min, probably not the main killer).
"压缩 56% → 上下文丢失 → 丢失生存状态 → 死亡" — plausible but the mechanism is your compression implementation dropping state, not compression per se. Compression itself doesn't kill; losing pinned state + blocking loop does.
Missing link in the chain: latency. The dominant cause is round-trip time. Neither 56% nor BEGIN_ARRAY alone explains 5 deaths; the AFK windows do. You should verify with timing data: measure per-turn latency old vs new model. If new model turns are ~30s and deaths occur during those windows → confirmed.
